reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and adds shared predicates (skipsWeekendOccurrences, isNonWorkingDay), but no shared function decides skip-versus-move, so each consumer composes the rule itself.

duplication.why: The 'daily skip: drop non-working day, else if skipWeekend move it' decision is written out separately in getNextDate, schedule-template, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and firstWeekdayOccurrence/lastWeekdayOccurrence are near-copies.

placement.why: Predicates and the holiday-aware move sit correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the composed weekend rule lives in each server caller.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps, with tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Every path now handles daily skips and holidays consistently today, but a future change to the rule must be repeated in four places with slightly different shapes (filter loop, continue, guard flag, closure).

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts), createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) and getNextDate each wrap getDateWithSkippedWeekend in their own skipsWeekendOccurrences/isNonWorkingDay branching instead of one shared weekend-rule function.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-or-move decision reappears as a push/filter loop in getUpcomingDates, an if/continue in getDatesInRange, resolveDate/isSkippedOccurrence closures in schedule-template, and a !skipsDailyWeekends guard plus firstWeekdayOccurrence in getNextDate.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; the daily special case is kept outside it and re-applied at getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and createScheduleList.
